source.title: Ulster Herald, 9 May 1936, p. 5 ("Nominations in Tyrone: the Omagh gerrymander")
source.publisher: Ulster Herald (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: Original citation restored 6 Nov 2026 (the 5 Nov verification had moved it because of a text-cleaning fault).

note: Triennial election of the rural district councillors. Nominations were received on 5 May 1936. Eleven divisions were filled unopposed; no nominations were received in Errigal, Fivemiletown, Foremass and Newtownsaville, whose sitting members were deemed re-elected (Irish News, 6 May 1936, p. 7), and Cullamore was contested between the sitting member, Mr. James E. Hackett, and Mr. James Gormley, another Nationalist (Belfast News-Letter, 6 May 1936, p. 9). The Cullamore result has not been found, so Cullamore is not recorded. Filed on 1936-06-03, the Tyrone polling day (previously filed under 1936-05-28, 6 Nov 2026). Returned unopposed.
